audit_findings.title: The operating numerator is stale despite known FY2026 cyber disruption
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025-based OE anchor feeds every scenario, while FY2026 incident costs, insurance recoveries, sales effects, and margins are absent from the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of the incident, we anticipate near-term disruption to our sales cycles with demand impacts more pronounced in the early part of the fiscal year and normalizing in the second half of the fiscal year 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated, but persistent impairment is not. Through June 2026, revenue increased $221.260 million and operating income increased $46.176 million year over year despite $26.5 million of incident-response costs and $5.3 million of insurance recoveries, a computed net incident cost of $21.2 million. The filing does not provide FY2026 owner earnings or isolate delayed sales, so the effect on normalized OE remains unquantified and could raise or lower value.
audit_findings.action: Compute FY2026 year-to-date OE using the existing methodology, reconcile the $26.5 million costs and $5.3 million recovery, and rerun the valuation after classifying sales disruption and remediation costs as temporary or recurring.

audit_findings.title: Adding all cash may double-count deferred-revenue float
audit_findings.magnitude: $1,605.782 million bridge addition exposed, equal to $27.58 per share and 17.7% of base equity value; June 2026 deferred revenue was $2,192.698 million; required reserve unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash collected before performance is added through the equity bridge and may be counted again through future accrual earnings if OE projections omit the associated working-capital reversal and cost of satisfying remaining obligations.
audit_findings.evidence: The composition of unsatisfied performance obligations consists mainly of deferred service revenue, and to a lesser extent, deferred product revenue, for which the Company has an obligation to perform, and has not yet recognized as revenue in the consolidated financial statements.
audit_findings.explanation: Adding the entire cash balance is demonstrated, but double counting is conditional on the OE working-capital treatment, which is not supplied. The exposed bridge amount is large relative to the $9,096 million base equity value, so even a partial operating-float reserve could materially change per-share value.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the historical and projected OE workpapers for deferred-revenue and unbilled-receivable movements; quantify cash needed to satisfy the $2,192.698 million deferred-revenue obligation and rerun the bridge using demonstrably excess cash only.

audit_findings.title: Uncertain-tax liabilities are a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $72.7 million of June 2026 unrecognized tax benefits, equal to 0.8% of base equity value or $1.25 per share; June income taxes payable were $66.829 million
audit_findings.mechanism: An outstanding tax reserve would reduce the cash available to common equity because settlement of an already accrued claim may not reduce future projected OE.
audit_findings.evidence: As of September 30, 2025, we had approximately $99.3 million of tax liabilities, including interest and penalties, related to uncertain tax positions (See Note 8 to our Consolidated Financial Statements).
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing establishes a tax exposure, although the eventual settlement is uncertain. Using the larger disclosed $72.7 million amount as the scale, a full deduction is only 0.8% of the $9,096 million base value and cannot bridge the $234.25 per-share gap between the $156.22 base value and the $390.47 market price.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $72.7 million gross unrecognized-tax-benefit balance to the $66.829 million income-tax payable balance, accrued interest and penalties, and any bridge reserve; deduct the confirmed non-operating settlement claim.

audit_findings.title: Unaccrued litigation could be an omitted common-equity claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured damages, settlements, royalties, defense costs, or regulatory payments would reduce future OE or require a direct equity-bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has not recorded any accrual for loss contingencies associated with such legal proceedings or the investigations discussed above.
audit_findings.explanation: The proceedings, including the continuing NGINX claim and FY2026 securities and derivative litigation, are demonstrated, but no loss is accrued and the company cannot estimate a possible-loss range. Consequently, omission of a claim is only a possibility, and the record cannot establish whether it is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the latest procedural status, counsel probability assessments, possible-loss ranges, defense-cost forecast, and applicable insurance limits and exclusions; probability-weight recurring costs in OE and reserve non-operating claims in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The purported share-count ceiling may omit post-year-end awards
audit_findings.magnitude: 81,099 identified RSUs, equal to 0.14% of 58.22917 million shares and at most approximately $0.19-$0.25 per share across the stated scenarios if entirely incremental; total unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional unvested equity claims increase the fully diluted share denominator and reduce value per share.
audit_findings.evidence: On October 31, 2025, the Company’s Board of Directors and Talent and Compensation Committee approved 81,099 RSUs to be granted to executive officers pursuant to the Company’s annual equity awards program.
audit_findings.explanation: The disclosed executive award alone is not material, but the supplied denominator lacks a September-to-June award roll-forward, so the record cannot determine the total omitted grants or distinguish them from awards already vested into outstanding shares. The identified grant is small, while the aggregate denominator effect remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Roll every award from September 2025 through June 2026, reconciling grants, vesting, forfeitures, withholding shares, repurchases, options, and performance-payout assumptions, and rerun per-share values with no double counting.

audit_findings.title: CalypsoAI creates a mixed operating perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: $145.207 million purchase price, equal to 1.6% of base equity value or $2.49 per valuation share; operating contribution was filed as not material
audit_findings.mechanism: The June 2026 cash bridge includes the acquisition payment, while the FY2025 OE history includes only four days of CalypsoAI; omitted normalized earnings could raise or lower OE depending on the acquired operation's profitability and integration costs.
audit_findings.evidence: On September 26, 2025, the Company closed on a transaction for the acquisition of CalypsoAI Corp. ("CalypsoAI"), a provider in enterprise AI security for $ 145.2 million in cash, with CalypsoAI immediately becoming a wholly-owned subsidiary of F5 upon the closing of the transaction.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is real, but the acquisition price is only 1.6% of the $9,096 million base value and both the 2025 10-K and June 2026 10-Q state that CalypsoAI's operating impact was not material. On the filed record, it is not capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Document CalypsoAI's FY2026 revenue, operating costs, integration spending, eligible amortization, and maintenance capital; adjust normalized OE only if the separated results contradict the filed immateriality assessment.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.3 million in FY2023 and $33.3 million in FY2024; the FY2024 amount equals 6.2% of the $533.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual D&A proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to historical OE and could increase the trend anchor and scenario values.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2023 $30.3m (26.9% of filed D&A); FY2024 $33.3m (31.1% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: There is no demonstrated overstatement: the unidentified amount remains an expense. Even the larger disclosed residual is 6.2% of the anchor, while the market price exceeds the $179.35 bull value by $211.12 per share, or 117.7%. This scale cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Classify the residual D&A from filed asset and amortization schedules and rerun the trend anchor only for amounts affirmatively shown to be eligible non-economic add-backs.
